newsitem.title: EGYPT: Hoechst Orient in 30 mln pound Egypt bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst Orient in 30 mln pound Egypt bond issue.

text.p: The Egyptian-German joint venture Hoechst Orient SAE on Thursday invited investors to subscribe to 300,000 five-year non-convertible bonds worth 10 pounds each during the month starting December 8.
The interest, variable and payable at six-month intervals, will be 0.25 percentage points above the average rate for six-month treasury bills, now about 10.198 percent.

Subscription fees will be two pounds per bond for holdings of up to 100 bonds, one pound per bond for holdings of between 100 and 1,000 bonds and 0.50 pounds per bond for holdings of more than 1,000 bonds.
The Cairo branch of National Soceite Generale Bank SAE is underwriting the 30 million pound issue, which is open to foreigners.

This is the second corporate bond issue by Hoechst Orient SAE, in which German pharmaceutical company Hoechst AGhas a 72 percent stake. The first issue in 1994 was the first corporate bond issue in more than four decades and was three times oversubscribed.
Egypt's Capital Market Authority authorised the bond issue in 1994, in line with economic reforms aimed at reversing decades of nationalisation an state control over firms.
On the interest rate set for its bond, Hoechst said that if there were no six-month treasury bills at the time of interest payment, the rate will be 11 percent.
